description: The leads the game proposes: lines of inquiry the player may investigate (docs/case-format.md, Leads). One per line: `text` (plain words, never ahead of the story), `source` (its quotes; a lead is proposed once they are read and its `needs` are held), `scores` (the NOTICE thought it scores for when investigated before Holmes's paragraph; null for a lead that scores nothing), `answer` and `answer_source` (what the story answers, shown once Holmes has taken the lead up and its quotes are read).

leads.text: Why was Silver Blaze led out onto the moor?
source: there were abundant proofs in the mud
leads.answer: He was to be lamed by a nick to a tendon, and so spirited a horse would have roused the soundest sleeper: it had to be done in the open air.
answer_source: It was absolutely necessary to do it in the open air

leads.text: Why curried mutton for Hunter's supper?
source: his supper, which consisted of a dish of curried mutton
leads.answer: Curry hid the taste of the powdered opium, and only Straker and his wife could have chosen it for supper that night.
answer_source: A curry was exactly the medium which would disguise this taste

leads.text: Why was Straker's overcoat on a furze-bush?
source: John Straker’s overcoat was flapping from a furze-bush
leads.answer: Straker took it off himself, in spite of the rain, to do his delicate task.
answer_source: taken off his overcoat in order to do his delicate task

leads.text: Why did Straker carry a tallow candle?
leads.answer: He needed a light for his work, struck in a hollow where it would not be seen.
answer_source: that was why he needed the candle, and struck the match
a hollow where his light would be invisible

leads.text: Why did Straker have a cataract knife?
source: It is what we call a cataract knife
leads.answer: It was for a delicate operation: a slight nick on the tendons of the horse's ham, to lame him without a trace.
answer_source: make a slight nick upon the tendons of a horse’s ham

leads.text: Why did Straker carry a bill made out to William Derbyshire?
source: made out by Madame Lesurier, of Bond Street, to William Derbyshire
leads.answer: Straker was William Derbyshire: he led a double life and kept a second establishment.
answer_source: Straker was leading a double life
dispose of the mythical Derbyshire

leads.text: Who were the clothes on the milliner's account for?
source: a milliner’s account for thirty-seven pounds fifteen
leads.answer: Straker's other wife, who had expensive tastes and plunged him into debt.
answer_source: who had a very dashing wife, with a strong partiality for expensive dresses
plunged him over head and ears in debt

leads.text: Why have the odds on Silver Blaze shortened?
source: the price has become shorter and shorter
leads.answer: Somebody knew the horse would run: Holmes had found him and ran him as he was sent over.
answer_source: took the liberty of running him just as he was sent over

leads.text: What was in the paper the stranger offered the maid?
source: He took a piece of white paper folded up out of his
leads.answer: A ten-pound note, Simpson says; one was found in his purse.
answer_source: He says that it was a ten-pound note
One was found in his

leads.text: What made the wound on Straker's head?
source: by repeated blows, have inflicted the terrible injuries
leads.answer: The horse lashed out when Straker struck a light behind him, and the steel shoe struck Straker full on the forehead.
answer_source:
the steel shoe had
      struck Straker full on the forehead

leads.text: Why did Fitzroy Simpson bet five thousand pounds against the favourite?
source: bets to the amount of five thousand
leads.answer: He made his living by book-making; and the curry rules him out of the case.
answer_source: doing a little quiet and genteel book-making
eliminated from the case

leads.text: Why did the gypsies break camp on Tuesday?
leads.answer: People like them clear out at any trouble, not to be pestered by the police; they could not hope to sell such a horse.
answer_source: These people always clear out when
They could not hope to sell such a horse

leads.text: What did the stranger want at King's Pyland?
leads.answer: Information about the King's Pyland horses and the second favourite, Simpson says: he had no sinister designs.
answer_source: obtain first-hand

leads.text: Why did Straker go down to the stables at one in the morning?
source: waking at one in the morning
leads.answer: On a dishonest errand: he took the horse out himself.
answer_source: went down to the stables in the dead of the night and took out
For a dishonest one, obviously

leads.text: Why was Straker holding the stranger's cravat?
source: clasped a red and black silk cravat
leads.answer: Simpson had dropped it as he fled, and Straker picked it up, perhaps to secure the horse's leg.
answer_source: he might use it in securing the horse

leads.text: Whose blood was on Straker's knife?
source: was clotted with blood up to the handle
leads.answer: His own: as he fell, the knife gashed his thigh.
answer_source: his knife gashed his thigh

leads.text: Why has nobody seen the horse?
leads.answer: Silas Brown came on him wandering at dawn, led him to Mapleton and hid him there.
answer_source: he perceived a strange horse wandering over the moor

leads.text: Why has the Colonel's horse not a white hair on him?
leads.answer: His face and leg had been coloured: wash them in spirits of wine and he is Silver Blaze.
answer_source: wash his face and his leg in spirits of wine
